entry.name: SubagentStop registered and closes a dispatch with no hand-written close
entry.expected: With the plugin installed, run a real Cadence dispatch, let it return, and issue NO hand-written `trace close`. `planning.mjs trace render --phase 2` shows that worker under `brackets` with a lifecycle `return` on .planning/trace.jsonl that no orchestrator step wrote.
entry.why_human: Out-of-reach resource, not an unexercised path: firing SubagentStop needs the host to dispatch and complete a subagent inside an installed plugin session, and this verifier has no live host session to dispatch from. Everything reachable was executed - piping a host-shaped payload into cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.mjs against a scratch project did append the close and did move the row from unpaired to brackets - so what remains unproven is only that the host invokes the registration, which no probe in this environment can trigger.

entry.name: A dispatch whose close never runs is still paired
entry.expected: After that same live dispatch, the worker appears under `brackets` and NOT under `unpaired`, and its bracket carries identity only (no tokens, turns or duration), which is the signature of a host-written close.
entry.why_human: Same out-of-reach resource. The record cannot witness it yet: the hook was registered mid-run, so both of this phase's own executor brackets were closed by the hand-written path and no bracket on .planning/trace.jsonl was written by the host. Only a real dispatch after this install can produce one.
